23/G.goal: Explain why XR systems are interactive systems guided by the disappearing-technology ideal and why HCI and human factors require designing them as user-centric systems for lay users with different characteristics.
23/G.achieves: It provides the conceptual foundation for the course's human-factors and user-experience topics, helping the learner understand the user perspective that should inform designing and implementing an XR system.

23/O1.goal: Frame XR as an interactive, disappearing technology oriented toward presence and explain why this means designers should accommodate lay users instead of requiring them to master the technology.
23/O1.achieves: It gives the learner an interactive-systems baseline for interpreting XR's human-factors and user-experience focus in later lectures.

23/O2.goal: Describe how human-computer interaction and human factors make interactive-system design user-centric by requiring interfaces to reflect user characteristics.
23/O2.achieves: It lets the learner evaluate XR interface and system-design choices using the user-centered criteria emphasized in the course.
